metadata.title: Implement Automatic Plan Adjustment for Early Completion

story.iWant: my study plan to automatically adjust when I complete a session ahead of schedule
story.soThat: I can make progress faster and optimize my study time.
story.tasks: - Enhance the frontend's `updateSessionStatus` handler to detect early completion. - If early completion is detected, make a `fire-and-forget` call to `POST /reschedule-plan` with `course_id` and `reason: "EARLY_COMPLETION"`. - Enhance the `ReschedulingService` in the FastAPI Backend to handle `reason: "EARLY_COMPLETION"`. - Implement logic to identify newly available time slots. - Implement logic to pull future 'Not Started' tasks into these slots. - Perform a bulk `UPDATE` on `scheduled_date` for affected `study_sessions` in Supabase. - Ensure the backend rescheduling algorithm considers the impact of early completion on future tasks. - Implement robust error handling and logging for this specific rescheduling scenario in the backend.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. When a user completes a study session ahead of schedule, the remaining 'Not Started' sessions for that course are automatically adjusted (AC2 from Tech Spec). - The adjustment logic should attempt to pull future tasks forward into newly available time slots. - This should also trigger the `POST /reschedule-plan` endpoint in the backend.

constraint.description: The rescheduling algorithm on the backend must complete in under 5 seconds, even for a course with hundreds of study sessions, when adjusting for early completion.
The algorithm should be optimized to minimize the number of database queries when adjusting for early completion (fetch upfront, calculate in memory, bulk update).
The `/reschedule-plan` endpoint must remain protected and verify that the requesting user owns the `course_id` when triggered by early completion.
The rescheduling algorithm must be transactional. If any part of it fails during early completion adjustment, the user's study plan should not be left in a corrupted state.
Log the execution time of the rescheduling algorithm when triggered by early completion. If the algorithm fails, log the error with `course_id` and plan state.
The adjustment logic must effectively utilize the current state of `study_sessions` (e.g., 'Not Started' status) and `courses` (e.g., `exam_date`) to pull future tasks forward.

tests.standards: Unit Tests (Backend): Create an extensive test suite for the rescheduling algorithm, focusing on early completion scenarios. Test with various inputs: plans with no room, ample room, varied task durations, etc. The algorithm should be testable in isolation. Integration Tests (Backend): Test the `/reschedule-plan` endpoint with `reason: "EARLY_COMPLETION"`, mocking the database to provide diverse plan states and verifying the correctness of `UPDATE` queries. E2E Tests: Simulate early completion of a study session in the frontend and verify that the calendar view on the dashboard updates automatically (via Realtime) to reflect the new, adjusted schedule (future tasks pulled forward).

ideas.idea: Simulate completing a study session ahead of schedule in the frontend and verify that a call to `POST /reschedule-plan` is made with `reason: "EARLY_COMPLETION"`.
Backend unit test for the rescheduling algorithm to ensure it correctly pulls future 'Not Started' sessions into newly available slots upon early completion.
E2E test: complete a session early, verify the dashboard updates automatically (via Realtime) to reflect the new schedule, with future tasks appearing earlier.
Profile the rescheduling algorithm with a large dataset (e.g., 200+ sessions) to ensure it meets the <5 second performance requirement for early completion adjustments.
